page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6e.large is a compute-optimized virtual server instance based on the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor with x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The hardware configuration provides 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs, with 1 thread per core. It is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU hardware, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the instance is positioned at the lower end of the compute spectrum. The single-core Geekbench score is average, placing in the middle 50%, while the multi-core Geekbench score falls into the bottom 10%. Similarly, stress-ng single-core CPU performance is weak, and multi-core performance is poor. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show poor performance, with read-only large block speeds at 12.97 GB/sec and write large block speeds at 11.91 GB/sec, both in the bottom 10%.

The instance supports advanced instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512 Foundation, and AVX-512 Vector Neural Network Instructions, alongside AES cryptography and BMI2 integer manipulation. Despite these hardware capabilities, Passmark CPU extended instructions and encryption tests score in the bottom 10%. Database operations and Redis SET operations also register in the bottom 10%, with Redis achieving 1.7 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.c6e.large offers dedicated CPU resources at a lower resource density, making it an entry-level option for workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation without high memory or storage demands. Given the benchmark results, the instance is best suited for lightweight workloads such as basic web serving, simple text processing, or low-throughput background tasks rather than intensive database operations or multi-threaded compilation.
